# Background

We conducted this experiment to study the effect of mmf1 mutants on Arabidopsis root microbiome composition and plant growth. We hypothesized that *mmf1-2* mutants would show altered root microbiome composition and growth compared to wild-type plants. We grew Arabidopsis plants on BXplus and BXminus soils and phenotyped them for rosette area and weighed them at the end of the experiment. We extracted the phenotypes using ARADEEPOPSIS and analyzed the root microbiome composition using amplicon sequencing for 16S rRNA, ITS fungal and ITS oomyctes. We used hamPCR according to @lundberg2021.

# Materials and methods

Plant lines used: WT (Col-0), *mmf1-1*, *mmf1-2*

-   **Purpose**: To study the effect of mmf1 mutants on Arabidopsis root microbiome composition and plant growth.

# Important results

-   **Plant growth**: The *mmf1-2* mutants showed a significant reduction in rosette area compared to the wild-type plants across the soils. *mmf1-2* mutants fail to show the BX-growth promotion phenotype.

-   **Microbiome composition**: The root microbiome composition of *mmf1-2* mutants was significantly different from the wild-type plants for bacteria on the BXplus microbiome. The *mmf1-2* mutants did not show a significant reduction in bacterial diversity compared to the wild-type plants. The fungal and oomycetes diversity was not significantly different between the plant lines.

## Prepare data

Purpose: Design Data Preparation: Imports and cleans the design file, assigning custom colors for visualization and filtering out unnecessary samples. Data Filtering: Filters the data to focus on bacteria, fungi, and oomycetes taxa and ensures unique sample numbers.

```{r}
# Import the design file that contains experimental design details
DESIGN <- read_excel(paths$DESIGN, sheet = "Sheet1")

# Filter out SYNCOM9 samples from the design data
DESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$sub_libr != "syncom9", ]

# Ensure the 'line' column is a factor and remove rows with missing 'line' values
DESIGN$line <- factor(DESIGN$line, levels = c("WT", "159", "318"))
DESIGN <- DESIGN[!is.na(DESIGN$line), ]

# Assign custom colors to lines for visualization purposes
DESIGN$cols_line <- NA
DESIGN$cols_line[DESIGN$line == "WT"] <- "#01686c"
DESIGN$cols_line[DESIGN$line == "159"] <- "#48afb3"
DESIGN$cols_line[DESIGN$line == "318"] <- "#e3913e"

# Create a collapsed color vector for the lines
temp <- data.frame(DESIGN$line, DESIGN$cols_line)
temp <- plyr::ddply(temp, .variables = "DESIGN.cols_line", .fun = unique)
level_cols_line <- as.character(temp[, 2])
names(level_cols_line) <- temp[, 1]
rm(temp)

# Assign colors based on experimental conditions (plus/minus)
DESIGN$cols_condition <- NA
DESIGN$cols_condition[DESIGN$condition == "minus"] <- "gold"
DESIGN$cols_condition[DESIGN$condition == "plus"] <- "seagreen"

# Collapse condition color vectors similarly
temp <- data.frame(DESIGN$condition, DESIGN$cols_condition)
temp <- plyr::ddply(temp, .variables = "DESIGN.cols_condition", .fun = unique)
level_cols_condition <- as.character(temp[, 2])
names(level_cols_condition) <- temp[, 1]

# Filter out unscaled and duplicate samples
DESIGN <- DESIGN[!(grepl("unscaled", DESIGN$sub_libr, fixed = TRUE)), ]
DESIGN <- DESIGN[!(grepl("dupl_for_At", DESIGN$sub_libr, fixed = TRUE)), ]

# Assign taxa and split DESIGN into bacteria, fungi, and oomycetes
DESIGN$taxa[DESIGN$sub_libr == "oomycetes"] <- "oomycetes"
bDESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$taxa == "bacteria", ]
fDESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$taxa == "fungi", ]
oDESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$taxa == "oomycetes", ]

# Reassign sample numbers across taxa
if (all(bDESIGN$sample_nr == fDESIGN$sample_nr) &
    all(bDESIGN$sample_nr == oDESIGN$sample_nr)) {
  bDESIGN$sample_nr <- paste0("sample", 1:nrow(bDESIGN))
  fDESIGN$sample_nr <- paste0("sample", 1:nrow(fDESIGN))
  oDESIGN$sample_nr <- paste0("sample", 1:nrow(oDESIGN))
}
```

## Process ASV tables

Purpose: ASV Import: Imports and processes ASV tables for bacteria, fungi, and oomycetes. Data Cleanup: Adapts column/row names for consistency and removes OTUs with zero counts.

```{r}
# Import ASV tables for bacteria, fungi, and oomycetes
bCOUNT <- read.delim(paths$bcount, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t")
fCOUNT <- read.delim(paths$fcount, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t")
oCOUNT <- read.delim(paths$fcount, header = TRUE, row.names = 1, sep = "\t")

# Transpose the tables
bCOUNT <- t(bCOUNT)
fCOUNT <- t(fCOUNT)
oCOUNT <- t(oCOUNT)

# Adapt column and row names for consistency
colnames(bCOUNT) <- gsub("BS09_", "", colnames(bCOUNT))
rownames(bCOUNT) <- gsub("OTU", "bOTU", rownames(bCOUNT))
colnames(fCOUNT) <- gsub("BS09_", "", colnames(fCOUNT))
rownames(fCOUNT) <- gsub("OTU", "fOTU", rownames(fCOUNT))
colnames(oCOUNT) <- gsub("BS09_", "", colnames(oCOUNT))
rownames(oCOUNT) <- gsub("OTU", "oOTU", rownames(oCOUNT))

# Filter to match design file and remove zero-count OTUs
bCOUNT <- as.data.frame(bCOUNT[, match(bDESIGN$bc_ID, colnames(bCOUNT))])
bCOUNT <- bCOUNT[rowSums(bCOUNT) > 0, ]
fCOUNT <- as.data.frame(fCOUNT[, match(fDESIGN$bc_ID, colnames(fCOUNT))])
fCOUNT <- fCOUNT[rowSums(fCOUNT) > 0, ]
oCOUNT <- as.data.frame(oCOUNT[, match(oDESIGN$bc_ID, colnames(oCOUNT))])
oCOUNT <- oCOUNT[rowSums(oCOUNT) > 0, ]
```

## Data normalization

Purpose: Bacterial Taxonomy Import: Imports and cleans the bacterial taxonomy table, removing unwanted OTUs (Cyanobacteria, Mitochondria, etc.). Label Assignment: Defines labels for bacterial phyla and sets them as factors.

```{r}
# Import and clean bacterial taxonomy table
bTAXA <- read.table(paths$btaxa, row.names = 1, sep = "\t", blank.lines.skip = FALSE)
colnames(bTAXA) <- tolower(colnames(bTAXA))
bTAXA[is.na(bTAXA)] <- "unassigned"
rownames(bTAXA) <- gsub("OTU", "bOTU", rownames(bTAXA))
bTAXA <- bTAXA[rownames(bTAXA) %in% rownames(bCOUNT), ]

# Remove OTUs of certain taxonomic groups
ASVs_to_remove <- c(-which(bTAXA$phylum == "Cyanobacteria"),
                    -which(bTAXA$family == "Mitochondria"),
                    -which(is.na(bTAXA)))

# Keep relevant ASVs only and align ASV IDs
bTAXA <- bTAXA[ASVs_to_remove, ]
bCOUNT <- bCOUNT[rownames(bTAXA), ]
bTAXA$ASV_ID <- rownames(bTAXA)

# Define labels for Proteobacteria and set labels as factors
bTAXA$labels <- as.character(bTAXA$phylum)
bTAXA$labels[bTAXA$kingdom == "Eukaryota"] <- "Host"
bTAXA$labels <- as.factor(bTAXA$labels)
```

# Bacterial sequence filtering

Purpose: Filtering: Removes samples with fewer than 60,000 sequences and ASVs with zero sequences. Summary: Provides a summary of the remaining bacterial ASVs in terms of total sequences, min, max, median, and number of OTUs.

```{r}
# Initialize a dataframe to store summary statistics
df <- data.frame(sum = NA, min = NA, max = NA, median = NA, OTUs = NA)

# Define the threshold for low sequence numbers
threshold <- 60000

# Identify and remove samples with low sequence counts (below threshold)
samples_to_remove <- names(which(colSums(bCOUNT) < threshold))
print(paste(length(samples_to_remove), "samples removed due to low number of sequences (threshold <", threshold, ")"))

# Remove these samples from the bDESIGN and bCOUNT tables
bDESIGN <- bDESIGN[!(bDESIGN$bc_ID %in% samples_to_remove), ]
bCOUNT <- bCOUNT[, !(colnames(bCOUNT) %in% samples_to_remove)]

# Remove ASVs with zero counts across all samples
ASVs_to_remove <- names(which(rowSums(bCOUNT) == 0))
bCOUNT <- bCOUNT[!(rownames(bCOUNT) %in% ASVs_to_remove), ]
bTAXA <- bTAXA[!(rownames(bTAXA) %in% ASVs_to_remove), ]

# Summarize the remaining sequence data
df$sum <- sum(colSums(bCOUNT))
df$min <- min(colSums(bCOUNT))
df$max <- max(colSums(bCOUNT))
df$median <- median(colSums(bCOUNT))
df$OTUs <- nrow(bCOUNT)

# Output the summary
#pander(df)
kable(df, caption = "Read count: Bacteria",
      col.names = c("Total", "Min", "Max", "Median", "OTUs"))

# Clean up
rm(df, ASVs_to_remove, samples_to_remove, threshold)
```

# Remove Eukaryotic Contaminants

## Bacteria

Purpose: Sequence Mapping: Compares bacterial sequences to host sequences to detect and remove contaminant OTUs (eukaryotic).

```{r}
# Import At.GI amplicon sequences (host sequences)
AtSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$host_amplicon)
AtSEQ <- as.data.frame(AtSEQ)
colnames(AtSEQ) <- "seqs"

# Import bacterial sequences
bSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$bseq)
bSEQ <- as.data.frame(bSEQ)
colnames(bSEQ) <- "seqs"
rownames(bSEQ) <- gsub("OTU", "bOTU", rownames(bSEQ))

# Identify eukaryotic OTUs in bacterial data
eOTU <- rownames(bTAXA)[bTAXA$labels == "Host"]
eSEQ <- bSEQ[rownames(bSEQ) %in% eOTU, , drop = FALSE]

# Initialize a distance matrix for mapping sequences
distances <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(AtSEQ), ncol = nrow(eSEQ)), row.names = rownames(AtSEQ))
colnames(distances) <- rownames(eSEQ)

# Function to map sequences and calculate distances
map <- function(AtSEQ) {
  eSEQs_to_map <- data.frame(seqs = c(as.character(AtSEQ), as.character(eSEQ$seqs[i])))
  eSEQs_to_map <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(eSEQs_to_map$seqs)
  eSEQs_aln <- DECIPHER::AlignSeqs(eSEQs_to_map, processors = 1, verbose = FALSE)
  dist_all <- DECIPHER::DistanceMatrix(eSEQs_aln, processors = 1, verbose = FALSE)
  return(dist_all[1, 2])
}

# Calculate distances for all eukaryotic sequences
for (i in 1:nrow(eSEQ)) {
  distances[, i] <- apply(AtSEQ, 1, map)
}

# Calculate sequence similarities
similarities <- 1 - distances

# Add OTU abundance to the similarity matrix and output
similarities <- rbind(similarities, n_seqs = rowSums(bCOUNT[rownames(bCOUNT) %in% colnames(distances), ]))
pander(t(similarities))
kable(t(similarities), caption = "OTUs mapping to GIGANTEA",
      col.names = c("OTUs", "Similarity", "n_seqs"))

# Remove OTUs with similarity below 99%
OTUs_to_remove <- colnames(similarities)[similarities[1, ] < 0.99]
bCOUNT <- bCOUNT[!(rownames(bCOUNT) %in% OTUs_to_remove), ]
bTAXA <- bTAXA[!(rownames(bTAXA) %in% OTUs_to_remove), ]

# Remove OTUs with zero abundance after filtering
zeroOTUs_to_remove <- names(which(colSums(bCOUNT) == 0))
bCOUNT <- bCOUNT[, !(colnames(bCOUNT) %in% zeroOTUs_to_remove)]
bTAXA <- bTAXA[!(rownames(bTAXA) %in% zeroOTUs_to_remove), ]

# Report removed OTUs
if (length(OTUs_to_remove) > 0) {
  print(paste0("The following eukaryotic OTUs were removed: ", paste(OTUs_to_remove, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  print("No eukaryotic OTUs were removed")
}

# Clean up
rm(eSEQ, AtSEQ, similarities, OTUs_to_remove, zeroOTUs_to_remove, distances)
```

## Fungi

Purpose:

Importing Sequences: Loads host and fungal sequences from specified file paths. Filtering: Retains only those fungal sequences present in the taxonomy data (fTAXA). Identifying Contaminants: Detects eukaryotic OTUs (considered as potential contaminants) within the fungal dataset. Mapping and Similarity Calculation: Aligns each host sequence with fungal sequences to calculate pairwise distances and convert them into similarity scores. OTU Removal: Eliminates fungal OTUs that have less than 99% similarity to host sequences, effectively removing potential eukaryotic contaminants. Cleaning Up: Removes any OTUs with zero abundance post-filtering to ensure data integrity.

```{r}
# Import Host Amplicon Sequences
AtSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$host_amplicon)
AtSEQ <- as.data.frame(AtSEQ)
colnames(AtSEQ) <- "seqs"

# Import Fungal Sequences
fSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$fseq)
fSEQ <- as.data.frame(fSEQ)
colnames(fSEQ) <- "seqs"
rownames(fSEQ) <- gsub("OTU", "fOTU", rownames(fSEQ))  # Prefix OTU IDs with 'f' for Fungi

# Filter to Keep Only Fungal Sequences Present in Taxonomy Data
fSEQ <- fSEQ[rownames(fSEQ) %in% rownames(fTAXA), , drop = FALSE]

# Identify Eukaryotic OTUs (Hosts) in Fungal Data
eOTU <- rownames(fTAXA)[fTAXA$labels == "Host"]

# Extract Eukaryotic Sequences
eSEQ <- fSEQ[rownames(fSEQ) %in% eOTU, , drop = FALSE]

# Clean Up Unnecessary Variables
rm(fSEQ, eOTU)

### MAPPING ###

# Initialize a Data Frame to Store Pairwise Distances
distances <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(AtSEQ), ncol = nrow(eSEQ)), row.names = rownames(AtSEQ))
colnames(distances) <- rownames(eSEQ)

# Define a Mapping Function to Calculate Distance Between Host and Fungal Sequences
map <- function(AtSEQ_entry) {
  # Combine Host Sequence and Current Fungal Sequence
  eSEQs_to_map <- data.frame(seqs = c(as.character(AtSEQ_entry), as.character(eSEQ$seqs[i])))
  
  # Convert to DNAStringSet for Alignment
  eSEQs_to_map <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(eSEQs_to_map$seqs)
  
  # Align Sequences
  eSEQs_aln <- DECIPHER::AlignSeqs(eSEQs_to_map, processors = 1, verbose = FALSE)
  
  # Compute Distance Matrix
  dist_all <- DECIPHER::DistanceMatrix(eSEQs_aln, processors = 1, verbose = FALSE)
  
  # Return the Distance Between Host and Fungal Sequence
  return(dist_all[1, 2])
}

# Calculate Distances for All Eukaryotic Sequences
for (i in 1:nrow(eSEQ)) {
  distances[, i] <- apply(AtSEQ, 1, map)
}

# Compute Similarity Scores
similarities <- 1 - distances

# Append OTU Abundance to Similarity Matrix
similarities <- rbind(similarities, n_seqs = rowSums(fCOUNT[rownames(fCOUNT) %in% colnames(distances), ]))

# Display the Similarity Matrix
#pander(t(similarities))
kable(t(similarities), caption = "OTUs mapping to GIGANTEA",
      col.names = c("OTUs", "Similarity", "n_seqs"))

# Identify and Remove OTUs with Similarity Below 99%
OTUs_to_remove <- colnames(similarities)[similarities[1, ] < 0.99]
fCOUNT <- fCOUNT[!(rownames(fCOUNT) %in% OTUs_to_remove), ]
fTAXA <- fTAXA[!(rownames(fTAXA) %in% OTUs_to_remove), ]

# Further Remove OTUs with Zero Abundance After Filtering
zeroOTUs_to_remove <- names(which(colSums(fCOUNT) == 0))
fCOUNT <- fCOUNT[, !(colnames(fCOUNT) %in% zeroOTUs_to_remove)]
fTAXA <- fTAXA[!(rownames(fTAXA) %in% zeroOTUs_to_remove), ]

# Report Removed OTUs
if (length(OTUs_to_remove) > 0) {
  print(paste0("The following eukaryotic OTUs were removed: ", paste(OTUs_to_remove, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  print("No eukaryotic OTUs were removed")
}

# Clean Up Temporary Variables
rm(eSEQ, AtSEQ, similarities, OTUs_to_remove, zeroOTUs_to_remove, distances)
```

## Oomycetes

Purpose:

Importing Sequences: Loads host sequences and reuses the fungal dataset (paths\$fseq) for Oomycetes analysis. Filtering: Retains only those oomycetal sequences present in the taxonomy data (oTAXA). Identifying Contaminants: Detects eukaryotic OTUs (considered as potential contaminants) within the oomycetal dataset. Mapping and Similarity Calculation: Aligns each host sequence with oomycetal sequences to calculate pairwise distances and convert them into similarity scores. OTU Removal: Eliminates oomycetal OTUs that have less than 99% similarity to host sequences, effectively removing potential eukaryotic contaminants. Cleaning Up: Removes any OTUs with zero abundance post-filtering to ensure data integrity.

```{r}
# Import Host Amplicon Sequences
AtSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$host_amplicon)
AtSEQ <- as.data.frame(AtSEQ)
colnames(AtSEQ) <- "seqs"

# Import Oomycetal Sequences (Same Dataset as Fungi)
oSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$fseq)  # Reusing the fungal dataset for Oomycetes
oSEQ <- as.data.frame(oSEQ)
colnames(oSEQ) <- "seqs"
rownames(oSEQ) <- gsub("OTU", "oOTU", rownames(oSEQ))  # Prefix OTU IDs with 'o' for Oomycetes

# Filter to Keep Only Oomycetal Sequences Present in Taxonomy Data
oSEQ <- oSEQ[rownames(oSEQ) %in% rownames(oTAXA), , drop = FALSE]

# Identify Eukaryotic OTUs (Hosts) in Oomycetal Data
eOTU <- rownames(oTAXA)[oTAXA$labels == "Host"]

# Extract Eukaryotic Sequences
eSEQ <- oSEQ[rownames(oSEQ) %in% eOTU, , drop = FALSE]

# Clean Up Unnecessary Variables
rm(oSEQ, eOTU)

### MAPPING ###

# Initialize a Data Frame to Store Pairwise Distances
distances <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(AtSEQ), ncol = nrow(eSEQ)), row.names = rownames(AtSEQ))
colnames(distances) <- rownames(eSEQ)

# Define a Mapping Function to Calculate Distance Between Host and Oomycetal Sequences
map <- function(AtSEQ_entry) {
  # Combine Host Sequence and Current Oomycetal Sequence
  eSEQs_to_map <- data.frame(seqs = c(as.character(AtSEQ_entry), as.character(eSEQ$seqs[i])))
  
  # Convert to DNAStringSet for Alignment
  eSEQs_to_map <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(eSEQs_to_map$seqs)
  
  # Align Sequences
  eSEQs_aln <- DECIPHER::AlignSeqs(eSEQs_to_map, processors = 1, verbose = FALSE)
  
  # Compute Distance Matrix
  dist_all <- DECIPHER::DistanceMatrix(eSEQs_aln, processors = 1, verbose = FALSE)
  
  # Return the Distance Between Host and Oomycetal Sequence
  return(dist_all[1, 2])
}

# Calculate Distances for All Eukaryotic Sequences
for (i in 1:nrow(eSEQ)) {
  distances[, i] <- apply(AtSEQ, 1, map)
}

# Compute Similarity Scores
similarities <- 1 - distances

# Append OTU Abundance to Similarity Matrix
similarities <- rbind(similarities, n_seqs = rowSums(oCOUNT[rownames(oCOUNT) %in% colnames(distances), ]))

# Display the Similarity Matrix
#pander(t(similarities))
kable(t(similarities), caption = "OTUs mapping to GIGANTEA",
      col.names = c("OTUs", "Similarity", "n_seqs"))
# Identify and Remove OTUs with Similarity Below 99%
OTUs_to_remove <- colnames(similarities)[similarities[1, ] < 0.99]
oCOUNT <- oCOUNT[!(rownames(oCOUNT) %in% OTUs_to_remove), ]
oTAXA <- oTAXA[!(rownames(oTAXA) %in% OTUs_to_remove), ]

# Further Remove OTUs with Zero Abundance After Filtering
zeroOTUs_to_remove <- names(which(colSums(oCOUNT) == 0))
oCOUNT <- oCOUNT[, !(colnames(oCOUNT) %in% zeroOTUs_to_remove)]
oTAXA <- oTAXA[!(rownames(oTAXA) %in% zeroOTUs_to_remove), ]

# Report Removed OTUs
if (length(OTUs_to_remove) > 0) {
  print(paste0("The following eukaryotic OTUs were removed: ", paste(OTUs_to_remove, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  print("No eukaryotic OTUs were removed")
}

# Clean Up Temporary Variables
rm(eSEQ, AtSEQ, similarities, OTUs_to_remove, zeroOTUs_to_remove, distances)
```

# Sequencing depth

## Function for Boxplot of Sequencing Depth

Purpose: `seq_nr_plot`\` This function creates a boxplot for sequencing depth across conditions and lines, displayed on a log2 scale. It uses jitter to display individual points. samples_plot: This function creates a barplot for sequencing depth per sample, grouped by condition and line.

```{r}
seq_nr_plot <- function(df, title = ""){
  seq_nr <- ggplot(data = df, aes(x = condition, y = col_sum, fill = line)) + 
              geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge2(width = 0.75, preserve = "single"), outlier.colour = NA) +
              geom_jitter(aes(col = line, group = line), size = 1, position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.2, dodge.width = 0.75)) +
              facet_grid(. ~ condition, scales = 'free_x', space = "free") +
              theme_bw() +
              theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 5)) +
              ylab("log2(seq)") +
              scale_fill_manual(values = level_cols_line) +
              scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_line) +
              scale_y_continuous(trans = 'log2') +
              ggtitle(title)
  return(seq_nr)
}

# Function for Barplot of Sequencing Depth by Sample
samples_plot <- function(df){
  samples <- ggplot(df, aes(x = x, y = col_sum, fill = line, color = line)) +
               geom_bar(width = 1, linewidth = 0.1, stat = "identity", col = "black", lty = 0.5) +
               scale_fill_manual(values = level_cols_line) +
               scale_colour_manual(values = level_cols_line) +
               xlab("samples") +
               ylab("seq / samples") +
               facet_grid(. ~ condition, scales = 'free_x', space = "free") +
               theme_bw() +
               theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
                     strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text.x = element_blank(),
                     legend.position = "none")
  return(samples)
}
```

# Rarefaction Analysis

## Bacteria Sequencing Depth Test

Explanation: Group Factor: Groups the bacteria samples by combining the line and condition columns from bDESIGN. Sequencing Depth Calculation: Computes the total number of sequences for each sample. Kruskal-Wallis Test: Tests if sequencing depth differs significantly between the groups. Rarefaction Threshold: Determines the minimum sequencing depth for rarefaction, rounded down to the nearest 100.

```{r}
# Bacteria Sequencing Depth Test

# Create group factor by concatenating line and condition for each sample
group <- paste(bDESIGN$line, bDESIGN$condition, sep = "_") %>% as.factor

# Calculate sequencing depth for each sample
sample_depth <- colSums(bCOUNT)

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis Test for differences in sequencing depth between groups
DAT_krusk <- coin::kruskal_test(sample_depth ~ group)
DAT_krusk  # Display test results

# Determine rarefaction threshold (minimum sequencing depth rounded down to nearest 100)
brare_threshold <- floor(min(sample_depth) / 100) * 100
brare_threshold  # Display rarefaction threshold

# Clean up
rm(group, sample_depth, DAT_krusk)


```

## Fungi Sequencing Depth Test

Explanation: Similar to the bacteria section, this test is applied to the fungi dataset to check for differences in sequencing depth between groups. Rarefaction Threshold: The rarefaction threshold for fungi is calculated based on the minimum sequencing depth.

```{r}
# Fungi Sequencing Depth Test

# Create group factor by concatenating line and condition for each sample
group <- paste(fDESIGN$line, fDESIGN$condition, sep = "_") %>% as.factor

# Calculate sequencing depth for each sample
sample_depth <- colSums(fCOUNT)

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis Test for differences in sequencing depth between groups
DAT_krusk <- coin::kruskal_test(sample_depth ~ group)
DAT_krusk  # Display test results

# Determine rarefaction threshold (minimum sequencing depth rounded down to nearest 100)
frare_threshold <- floor(min(sample_depth) / 100) * 100
frare_threshold  # Display rarefaction threshold

# Clean up
rm(group, sample_depth, DAT_krusk)
```

## Oomycetes Sequencing Depth Test

Explanation: The same process is applied to the oomycetes dataset, testing for differences in sequencing depth between groups and determining the rarefaction threshold.

```{r}
# Oomycetes Sequencing Depth Test

# Create group factor by concatenating line and condition for each sample
group <- paste(oDESIGN$line, oDESIGN$condition, sep = "_") %>% as.factor

# Calculate sequencing depth for each sample
sample_depth <- colSums(oCOUNT)

# Perform Kruskal-Wallis Test for differences in sequencing depth between groups
DAT_krusk <- coin::kruskal_test(sample_depth ~ group)
DAT_krusk  # Display test results

# Determine rarefaction threshold (minimum sequencing depth rounded down to nearest 100)
orare_threshold <- floor(min(sample_depth) / 100) * 100
orare_threshold  # Display rarefaction threshold

# Clean up
rm(group, sample_depth, DAT_krusk)
```

**Conclusion:** Because there are significant differences between the treatments in bacteria, we normalize the data by rarefication for diversity comparisions (see Weiss et al. (2017), Microbiome Journal). For consistency we do it for bacteria, fungi and oomycetes. We define the rarefaction threshold per sample to `r brare_threshold` for bacteria, `r frare_threshold` for fungi and `r orare_threshold` for oomycetes.

## Rarefaction

```{r}
# Bacteria Rarefaction
bCOUNT_norm <- t(vegan::rrarefy(t(bCOUNT), brare_threshold)) %>% as.data.frame()
bCOUNT_norm <- bCOUNT_norm[rowSums(bCOUNT_norm) > 0, ]  # Remove rows with 0 sequences
bTAXA_norm <- bTAXA[rownames(bTAXA) %in% rownames(bCOUNT_norm), ]

# Fungi Rarefaction
fCOUNT_norm <- t(vegan::rrarefy(t(fCOUNT), frare_threshold)) %>% as.data.frame()
fCOUNT_norm <- fCOUNT_norm[rowSums(fCOUNT_norm) > 0, ]  # Remove rows with 0 sequences
fTAXA_norm <- fTAXA[rownames(fTAXA) %in% rownames(fCOUNT_norm), ]

# Oomycetes Rarefaction
oCOUNT_norm <- t(vegan::rrarefy(t(oCOUNT), orare_threshold)) %>% as.data.frame()
oCOUNT_norm <- oCOUNT_norm[rowSums(oCOUNT_norm) > 0, ]  # Remove rows with 0 sequences
oTAXA_norm <- oTAXA[rownames(oTAXA) %in% rownames(oCOUNT_norm), ]
```

# Outlier Detection

## Sample Control

We use the method CLOUD developped by Montassier et al. 2018, which is a non.parametric detection test for outliers. We perform the test with Bray-Curtis distances from the rarefied data for each substrate and each plastic treatment individually. We set the number of nearest neighbors to 60% of the samples size and chose an empirical outlier percentile of 0.1. We remove all outliers from our data.

```{r}
# Function to Detect Outliers
detect_outliers <- function(DESIGN, COUNT_norm, line) {
  
  # Subset the samples for the specified line
  samples_sub <- DESIGN$sample_name[DESIGN$line %in% line]
  
  # Subset the count matrix for the selected samples
  DAT_sub <- COUNT_norm[, colnames(COUNT_norm) %in% samples_sub]
  
  # Compute Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between the samples
  bdist <- vegdist(t(DAT_sub), method = "bray")
  
  # Set the number of nearest neighbors (60% of the sample size)
  k <- floor(ncol(DAT_sub) * 0.6)
  
  # Apply the CLOUD test from Montassier et al. 2018
  test <- piecewise_kn_V1(d = bdist, test.ix = colnames(DAT_sub), k = k)
  
  # Identify outliers (samples with p-values <= 0.1)
  outliers <- colnames(DAT_sub)[test[["pvals"]] <= 0.1]
  
  return(outliers)
}
```

## Outlier Detection

```{r}
# Detect Outliers for Bacteria, Fungi, and Oomycetes

# Bacteria
boutliers <- detect_outliers(DESIGN = bDESIGN, COUNT_norm = bCOUNT_norm, line = unique(bDESIGN$line))

# Fungi
foutliers <- detect_outliers(DESIGN = fDESIGN, COUNT_norm = fCOUNT_norm, line = unique(fDESIGN$line))

# Oomycetes
ooutliers <- detect_outliers(DESIGN = oDESIGN, COUNT_norm = oCOUNT_norm, line = unique(oDESIGN$line))
```

## Remove outliers for bacteria

```{r}
# Bacteria Outlier Removal

# Remove outliers from the design table
bDESIGN <- bDESIGN[!(bDESIGN$sample_name %in% boutliers),]

# Remove outliers from the normalized count matrix
bCOUNT_norm <- bCOUNT_norm[, !(colnames(bCOUNT_norm) %in% boutliers)]

# Identify and remove ASVs with zero counts across all samples
ASVs_to_remove <- names(which(rowSums(bCOUNT_norm) == 0))
bCOUNT_norm <- bCOUNT_norm[!(rownames(bCOUNT_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]

# Update the taxonomy table to remove ASVs with zero counts
bTAXA_norm <- bTAXA_norm[!(rownames(bTAXA_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]

```

# Beta diversity

# Background

We ge an overview of the microbial communitites between Col-0 and *mmf1-2* mutants grown on BXplus and BXminus soils. We perform alpha and beta diversity analysis to investigate the differences in the microbial communities between the different Arabidopsis lines and conditions. We use the Shannon index to calculate alpha diversity. We use the Kruskal-Wallis test to test the significance of the differences in alpha diversity between the different Arabidopsis lines and conditions. We use the Bray-Curtis distance metric for beta diversity analysis. We perform PERMANOVA to test the significance of the differences in beta diversity between the different Arabidopsis lines and conditions. We also perform CAP analysis to investigate the effects of line and condition on beta diversity.

# Setup

# Alpha Diversity

Prepare Count tables Prepare the count tables for the alpha diversity analysis by transposing the data to have samples as rows and OTUs/taxa as columns.

```{r}
# Prepare data for shannon indices

# Transpose data to have samples as rows and OTUs/taxa as columns
bCOUNT_filt_t <- t(bCOUNT_filt)
fCOUNT_filt_t <- t(fCOUNT_filt)
oCOUNT_filt_t <- t(oCOUNT_filt)
```

## Calculate Shannon index

Calculate the Shannon diversity index for the bacterial, fungal, and oomycete communities.

```{r}
# Calculate Shannon index using the vegan package
bSHANNON <- diversity(bCOUNT_filt_t, index="shannon")
fSHANNON <- diversity(fCOUNT_filt_t, index="shannon")
oSHANNON <- diversity(oCOUNT_filt_t, index="shannon")

# Print the calculated Shannon diversity indices
#print(bSHANNON)
#print(fSHANNON)
#print(oSHANNON)
```

## Alpha diversity Bacteria

Perform the Kruskal-Wallis test to test the significance of the differences in bacterial alpha diversity between the different Arabidopsis lines and conditions.

```{r}
# Step 1: Ensure bSHANNON is a data frame
if (!is.data.frame(bSHANNON)) {
  bSHANNON <- as.data.frame(bSHANNON)
}

# Step 2: Convert rownames to a column in bSHANNON
bSHANNON <- bSHANNON %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "sample_name")

# Step 3: Merge with bDESIGN_filt
merged_data <- merge(bSHANNON, bDESIGN_filt, by = "sample_name")

# Step 4: Calculate Kruskal-Wallis p-values for each condition
p_values <- merged_data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(p_value = kruskal.test(bSHANNON ~ line)$p.value)

# Print the p-values
#print(p_values)
kable(p_values, caption = "Shannon index: Bacteria",
      col.names = c("Microbiome", "p-value"))
```

## Plot - Bacteria

```{r}
#| label: fig-bSHANNON_plot
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: Shannon indices for bacteria.
#| include: false
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE)

# Create the boxplot with p-value annotations
bSHANNON_plot <- ggplot(
  merged_data, 
  aes(x = condition, y = bSHANNON, fill = condition, alpha = line)
) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +  # Boxplot with transparency
  geom_point(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), 
    size = 1.0, 
    aes(color = condition, shape = line)
  ) +  # Points with same fill as boxplot
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",  # Show legend at the bottom
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),  # Black border
    text = element_text(size = 7),             # Set all text elements to 7pt
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),       # Axis titles
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),        # Axis text
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),     # Legend titles
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),      # Legend text
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7),       # Plot title
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7)     # Plot subtitle
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 7)) +
  labs(
    title = "Shannon index - Bacteria", 
    x = "Condition", 
    y = "Shannon index", 
    fill = "Condition", 
    color = "Condition", 
    alpha = "Line"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("seagreen", "gold2")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("seagreen", "gold2")) +  # Points color matches boxplot fill
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(0.9, 0.5)) +  # Different alpha values for the lines
  stat_compare_means(
    method = "kruskal.test", 
    label = "p.signif", 
    label.y = max(merged_data$bSHANNON, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.8
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = p_values, 
    aes(
      x = condition, 
      y = max(merged_data$bSHANNON, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.1, 
      label = paste0("p = ", round(p_value, 3))
    ), 
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  )

bSHANNON_plot

# Save the plot
ggsave(
  filename = "bSHANNON_plot.pdf", 
  plot = bSHANNON_plot, 
  width = 14, 
  height = 10, 
  units = "cm", 
  path = "Output/figures/"
)
```

# Beta Diversity

We get an overview by investigating the full model to see which factors alters the beta diversity. We use the Bray-Curtis distance metric for beta diversity analysis. We perform PERMANOVA to test the significance of the differences in beta diversity between the different Arabidopsis lines and conditions.

## Permanova

```{r}
set.seed(100010)
#Bacteria
bdist <- vegdist(t(bCOUNT_filt), method="bray")
bdist_paov <- adonis2(bdist ~ line * condition, by = "terms", data=bDESIGN_filt)
#pander(bdist_paov, caption="PERMANOVA: Bacteria")
kable(bdist_paov, caption = "PERMANOVA: Bacteria",
      col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"))

#Fungi
fdist <- vegdist(t(fCOUNT_filt), method="bray")
fdist_paov <- adonis2(fdist ~ line * condition, by = "terms", data=fDESIGN_filt)
#pander(fdist_paov, caption="PERMANOVA: Fungi")
kable(fdist_paov, caption = "PERMANOVA: Fungi",
      col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"))

#Bacteria
odist <- vegdist(t(oCOUNT_filt), method="bray")
odist_paov <- adonis2(odist ~ line * condition, by = "terms", data=oDESIGN_filt)
#pander(odist_paov, caption="PERMANOVA: Oomycetes")
kable(odist_paov, caption = "PERMANOVA: Oomycetes",
      col.names = c("Term", "DF", "Sums of Squares", "Mean Squares", "F-Model", "P-Value"))
```

**Conclusion:** The bacterial communities are different between the different Arabidopsis-lines, between the different conditions but not their interaction. For fungi we find a difference between the conditions, but not between lines or their interactions. For oomycetes we only see community differences for the two conditions.

## Reduced Permanova

Compare Col-0 with mmf1 on the two soils. We use the Bray-Curtis distance metric for beta diversity analysis. We perform PERMANOVA to test the significance of the differences in beta diversity between Col-0 and *mmf1-2* on the different soils.


```{r}
#| eval: false
#| include: false
# Function to get centroid lines
centroid_lines <- function(PHYSEQ, dist_matrix, group, axes = c(1, 2)) {
  # Get ordination values
  lines <- as.data.frame(
    plot_ordination(PHYSEQ, dist_matrix, axes = axes, justDF = TRUE)
  )
  colnames(lines)[1:2] <- c("Axis.1", "Axis.2")
  lines <- lines[, colnames(lines) %in% c("Axis.1", "Axis.2", group)]  # Subset
  
  # Get centroids (means of each group)
  means1 <- aggregate(
    lines$Axis.1, 
    by = as.list(lines[, colnames(lines) %in% group, drop = FALSE]), 
    FUN = mean
  )
  means2 <- aggregate(
    lines$Axis.2, 
    by = as.list(lines[, colnames(lines) %in% group, drop = FALSE]), 
    FUN = mean
  )
  
  # Concatenate groups (for multiple groups)
  lines$concact <- lines[, colnames(lines) %in% group, drop = FALSE] %>%
    apply(2, as.character) %>%
    apply(1, paste, collapse = "")
  
  means1$concact <- means1[, colnames(means1) %in% group, drop = FALSE] %>%
    apply(2, as.character) %>%
    apply(1, paste, collapse = "")
  
  means2$concact <- means2[, colnames(means2) %in% group, drop = FALSE] %>%
    apply(2, as.character) %>%
    apply(1, paste, collapse = "")
  
  # Add means to data frame
  lines$Axis.1.means <- NA
  lines$Axis.2.means <- NA
  group_values <- unique(lines$concact)
  
  for (i in group_values) {
    lines$Axis.1.means[lines$concact == i] <- means1$x[means1$concact == i]
    lines$Axis.2.means[lines$concact == i] <- means2$x[means1$concact == i]
  }
  
  # Subset the data frame
  lines <- lines[, colnames(lines) %in% c("Axis.1", "Axis.2", "Axis.1.means", "Axis.2.means")]
  
  # Return the result
  return(lines)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-PCA_plot
#| eval: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: PCA plot for bacteria, fungi and oomycetes.
#| include: false
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE)
# Bacteria
bPCoA_bray <- ordinate(bPHYSEQ, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")
p0 <- plot_ordination(
  bPHYSEQ, 
  bPCoA_bray, 
  color = "condition", 
  shape = "line", 
  axes = c(1, 2)
)
blines <- centroid_lines(
  PHYSEQ = bPHYSEQ, 
  dist_matrix = bPCoA_bray, 
  group = c("condition", "line")
)
p0 <- p0 + 
  geom_segment(
    aes(xend = blines$Axis.1, yend = blines$Axis.2), 
    x = blines$Axis.1.means, 
    y = blines$Axis.2.means, 
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
  theme_bw()
fig_bac <- p0

# Fungi
fPCoA_bray <- ordinate(fPHYSEQ, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")
p0 <- plot_ordination(
  fPHYSEQ, 
  fPCoA_bray, 
  color = "condition", 
  shape = "line", 
  axes = c(1, 2)
)
flines <- centroid_lines(
  PHYSEQ = fPHYSEQ, 
  dist_matrix = fPCoA_bray, 
  group = c("condition", "line")
)
p0 <- p0 + 
  geom_segment(
    aes(xend = flines$Axis.1, yend = flines$Axis.2), 
    x = flines$Axis.1.means, 
    y = flines$Axis.2.means, 
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
  theme_bw()
fig_fun <- p0

# Oomycetes
oPCoA_bray <- ordinate(oPHYSEQ, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")
p0 <- plot_ordination(
  oPHYSEQ, 
  oPCoA_bray, 
  color = "condition", 
  shape = "line", 
  axes = c(1, 2)
)
olines <- centroid_lines(

  group = c("condition", "line")
)
p0 <- p0 + 
  geom_segment(
    aes(xend = olines$Axis.1, yend = olines$Axis.2), 
    x = olines$Axis.1.means, 
    y = olines$Axis.2.means, 
    alpha = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +

fig_oom <- p0

# Combine the plots
fig_5.1 <- plot_grid(
  fig_bac + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fig_fun + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(colour = ""),
  fig_oom + theme(legend.position = "none") + labs(colour = ""),
  labels = c("Bacteria", "Fungi", "Oomycetes"),
  align = "hv",
  nrow = 1

# Add legend

)

# Print and save
PCA_plot

)
```

## Prepare figure

We use the Constrained Analysis of Principal coordinates (CAP) to analyze the effects of line and condition on beta diversity for bacterial, fungal, and oomycete communities. We use the Bray-Curtis distance metric for beta diversity analysis.

```{r}
#| label: fig-CAP_plot
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| fig-cap: CAP plot for bacteria, fungi and oomycetes.
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE)

### Figure 5.2 | CAP - line and condition effect on beta diversity

# This script performs Constrained Analysis of Principal coordinates (CAP)
# on bacterial, fungal, and oomycete communities, analyzing the effects of 
# line and condition on beta diversity.

# Set plot dimensions
fig.height <- 6
fig.width <- 12

# ==============================
# Bacteria Analysis ---------------------------
# ==============================

# CAP ordination for Bacteria
CAP_bray <- ordinate(bPHYSEQ, method = "CAP", formula = ~ line * condition, distance = "bray")
CAP_bray_var_tbl <- variability_table(CAP_bray)  # Extract variation details

# Summarize abundance for the top 6 phyla
phylum.sum <- tapply(
  taxa_sums(bPHYSEQ), 
  tax_table(bPHYSEQ)[, "labels"], 
  sum, 
  na.rm = TRUE
)
topphyla <- names(sort(phylum.sum, decreasing = TRUE))[1:6]
phy_sub <- prune_taxa(
  tax_table(bPHYSEQ)[, "labels"] %in% topphyla, 
  bPHYSEQ
)

# Extract R2 and p-values for the subtitle
score <- paste(
  " ~ line * condition \n line: ",
  format(bdist_paov$R2[rownames(bdist_paov) == "line"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
  "% var, P=", format(bdist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(bdist_paov) == "line"], digits = 2),
  "\n condition: ",
  format(bdist_paov$R2[rownames(bdist_paov) == "condition"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
  "% var, P=", format(bdist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(bdist_paov) == "condition"], digits = 2),
  "\n line:condition: ",
  format(bdist_paov$R2[rownames(bdist_paov) == "line:condition"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
  "% var, P=", format(bdist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(bdist_paov) == "line:condition"], digits = 2)
)

# Plot ordination for Bacteria
p0 <- phyloseq::plot_ordination(phy_sub, CAP_bray, title = "Bacteria", axes = c(1, 2))
p0$layers <- p0$layers[-1]  # Remove default layer (points)
p0 <- p0 +
  stat_ellipse(
    geom = "polygon", type = "t", level = 0.95, size = 0.4,
    aes(group = condition, color = condition, fill = condition), 
    alpha = 0.01
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
  scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
  new_scale_color() +
  geom_point(aes(shape = factor(line), color = condition), size = 1.0) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 2)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = level_cols_condition) +
  labs(
    subtitle = score,
    color = "Microbiome", fill = "Microbiome", 
    shape = "Line", alpha = "Line"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 7),             # Set all text to 7pt
    axis.title = element_text(size = 7),       # Axis titles
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),        # Axis text
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),     # Legend titles
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),      # Legend text
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7),       # Plot title
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7)     # Plot subtitle
  )
fig_bac <- p0  # Save the plot

# ==============================
# Fungi and Oomycetes Analyses ---------------------------
# ==============================

# Repeat similar steps for Fungi and Oomycetes
process_CAP <- function(PHYSEQ, dist_paov, title, colors) {
  CAP_bray <- ordinate(PHYSEQ, method = "CAP", formula = ~ line * condition, distance = "bray")
  phylum.sum <- tapply(
    taxa_sums(PHYSEQ), 
    tax_table(PHYSEQ)[, "labels"], 
    sum, 
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
  topphyla <- names(sort(phylum.sum, decreasing = TRUE))[1:6]
  phy_sub <- prune_taxa(tax_table(PHYSEQ)[, "labels"] %in% topphyla, PHYSEQ)
  score <- paste(
    " ~ line * condition \n line: ",
    format(dist_paov$R2[rownames(dist_paov) == "line"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
    "% var, P=", format(dist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(dist_paov) == "line"], digits = 2),
    "\n condition: ",
    format(dist_paov$R2[rownames(dist_paov) == "condition"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
    "% var, P=", format(dist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(dist_paov) == "condition"], digits = 2),
    "\n line:condition: ",
    format(dist_paov$R2[rownames(dist_paov) == "line:condition"] * 100, digits = 2, nsmall = 1),
    "% var, P=", format(dist_paov$`Pr(>F)`[rownames(dist_paov) == "line:condition"], digits = 2)
  )
  p0 <- phyloseq::plot_ordination(phy_sub, CAP_bray, title = title, axes = c(1, 2))
  p0$layers <- p0$layers[-1]
  p0 <- p0 +
    stat_ellipse(
      geom = "polygon", type = "t", level = 0.95, size = 0.4,
      aes(group = condition, color = condition, fill = condition), 
      alpha = 0.01
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    new_scale_color() +
    geom_point(aes(shape = factor(line), color = condition), size = 1.0) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 2)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      subtitle = score,
      color = "Microbiome", fill = "Microbiome", 
      shape = "Line", alpha = "Line"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 7),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 7),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7)
    )
  return(p0)
}

fig_fun <- process_CAP(fPHYSEQ, fdist_paov, "Fungi", level_cols_condition)
fig_oom <- process_CAP(oPHYSEQ, odist_paov, "Oomycetes", level_cols_condition)

# ==============================
# Combine and Save Plots ---------------------------
# ==============================

# Combine all three figures
fig_5.2 <- plot_grid(
  fig_bac + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fig_fun + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  fig_oom + theme(legend.position = "none"),
  align = "hv", 
  nrow = 1
)

# Extract legend from the Bacteria plot
legend <- get_legend(fig_bac + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + labs(fill = "line"))

# Add legend to the combined plot
CAP_plot <- plot_grid(fig_5.2, legend, nrow = 2, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

print(CAP_plot)
# Save the combined plot
ggsave(
  "CAP_condition_color.pdf", 
  plot = CAP_plot, 
  width = 17.5, 
  height = 8, 
  units = "cm", 
  path = "Output/Figures/"
)
```

```{r}
}))
```
